methods.name: events
methods.description: Stream events. After the response the server writes one event per line (see Events) for the terminals carrying every one of `labels`, first those after `since` still kept (the last 4,096 events, and each terminal's last 256 `text` chunks before them), and never closes the connection; closing it unsubscribes. A client more than 4,096 events behind gets `{"jsonrpc":"2.0","method":"lagged","params":{"seq":N}}` and the connection is closed; it resumes with `since`. A connection that sent `heartbeat` gets `{"jsonrpc":"2.0","method":"heartbeat"}` lines when idle.

methods.name: run
methods.description: Start a terminal. `name` defaults to the first free `tN`; `keep` brings it back as a shell in its cwd after a server restart; `rows` and `cols` default to `$SHED_SIZE` (`RxC`) of the server, else 50x200. ACP: `mcp_servers` (stdio, `http`, `sse`, in ACP's shapes) go to the agent; their env and header values are never saved or shown. `meta` (an object) goes unchanged as the session's `_meta`. `no_hibernate` keeps the agent running when idle. `mem_max_mb` (default the server's `$SHED_MEM_MAX`, e.g. `4G`) limits the process tree's memory, and a `mem-limit` event (with `notify`, a `[shed] <name> mem-limit …` line to the parent) says what was ended: on Linux with a user systemd that has the memory controller the program runs in its own scope with `MemoryMax` and the kernel ends a process (the agent's children are ranked first); elsewhere, once the tree is over for two samples in a row, the sampler ends the largest process the agent started (SIGTERM, SIGKILL 2 s later), and an agent over it by itself is only reported. The sampler is a guard against sustained use, not a hard limit: a fast allocation can pass it between samples. `warm` takes the ready spare session of the same recipe (agent, command, cwd, policy, MCP servers, meta, size), renamed to `name` with these labels, and starts the next spare; spares are listed as `.warm-N`, at most `$SHED_WARM_MAX` (default 2) of them, each killed after `$SHED_WARM_IDLE` seconds (default 600) unused. `parent` links it to the terminal that started it: when the parent's program ends the child is killed too, unless `outlive`; with `notify` a `[shed] <name> blocked|error|exited …` line is typed into the parent (a prompt for an ACP parent) when the child blocks, errors or ends, once per piece of news, held while the parent reports `working`. `account` (ACP, on the main host) runs the agent on that account of its provider (`account.ls`): its folder variable set, its token too while its own login is signed out, none of the record's `scrub` and `cache.api_vars` inherited, and a caller `env` setting any of them refused; `meta` and the command are unchanged, and the token is kept in memory only.

TerminalInfo.description:
A terminal, as `run`, `ls`, `get`, `kill` and `rm` return it: `state` is `running` or `exited`; `exit` is the
exit status (128 + N for signal N), `null` while running or when the program was lost in a server restart;
`pid` is set while running; `reported` is the state the program last reported (absent until then), with OSC
7501's `kind`, `progress`, `app`, `title` and `msg` when it sent them, or `stuck` while the program has left
input unread for over a second (`send`, `keys` and `acp.model` then fail, their input queued); `records` are
its OSC 7501 reports with an `id`, one per id; `idle_after` is set when the `idle` fallback is on;
`resources` is the process tree's memory (MiB) and CPU (percent of one core) at the last sample, while
running; an ACP terminal's `session` is its agent session (`id`, for `run`'s `resume`; the current `model`
and the `models`, `[id, name]`; `run`'s `mcp_servers` with each env and header value as `***`; the agent's
slash `commands`, `[name, description, hint]`; its last `usage`: `used` and `size` of the context window in
tokens, and the `cost` when sent); `parent` names the terminal that started it (absent without one), with
`outlive` and `notify` as `run` set them; `redacted` (a login's terminal) means `read`, `screen.watch`,
`wait`'s `output` and its events show its text with anything like a token as `[redacted]`, and `attach` is refused;
`account` is the account it runs on.

Event.description:
An event names its terminal, carries its labels and its `parent` (absent without one) and counts up in
`seq`; `event` is `started`, `state` (the reported state changed), `exited` (by itself, with its `code`),
`killed` (by `kill`), `resources` (memory or CPU moved by more than 10 % since the last one) or `mem-limit`
(the tree passed `mem_max_mb`; `ended_by` is `kernel`, `shed` or `none`).

An ACP terminal (`shed run --acp`) adds its agent's events, emitted by its bridge: `turn` (a prompt), `text`
(a reply chunk), `tool_call` (started or changed), `plan`, `mode`, `approval_request` (answer with
`shed approve`), `approved`, `reply` (the turn's whole reply and its `stop_reason`), `session` (the session
is ready, or its model or slash commands changed) and `usage` (the agent's `usage_update`: tokens `used` of
the context window's `size`, and its `cost`). A resumed session's history (`run` with `resume`) comes first, from
shed's own transcript, its events marked `"replay": true` so a client does not count them as new; what the
agent replays is dropped. An idle agent hibernates (state `hibernated`, its processes stopped); the next
send wakes it on the same session.

ScreenUpdate.description:
`screen.watch` writes one update per line. `seq` is the screen's change count; `rows`, `cols`, `cursor`
(`[row, col]`, from 0) and `scrollback` (lines) are always there; `lines` holds the rows that changed, each
as runs of cells with one pen: `fg` and `bg` (a palette index 0–255, or `[r, g, b]`; `null` is the default),
`bold`, `italic`, `underline` and `inverse`. Trailing blank default cells are dropped, so a blank row has no
runs. `full` marks an update that carries every row: the first, and the one after a resize.

code.description: A shed error's name (`NO_SUCH_TERMINAL`), a guard's verdict (`GUARD_REFUSED`) or the limit (`FUEL`).

method.description: The shed method that failed or was refused.

ScriptError.description: A script's error: where, and what.

params.description: Its params, as the script gave them.

Acting.description:
One acting call: `result` when it was answered, `error` when the guard refused it, it failed or it was
still in flight when the run stopped (`CANCELLED`); never both. Over `REPLY_LIMIT` only `method` and
`error` (or `result: true`) are kept.

ActingError.description: Why an acting call came to nothing.

oneOf.description: No child is working: each has exited or reports something other than `working`.
The next child that reports `done`, `blocked` or `error`, or exits; the result names it.
A state in `until` or the `output` pattern matched.
The program exited first.
The timeout passed first.

title.description: The first prompt's first line, at most 80 characters.

updated.description: When its last turn ended, else when it started, unix seconds.

turns.description: How many turns it has had.

transcript.description: The transcript's path; filled in by `agents sessions`, not stored.

SessionRecord.description:
A session shed ran, `sessions/<id>.json` beside the state file: `agents sessions` lists these, `run
--resume <id>` continues one. Its transcript is `sessions/<id>.jsonl`; in a file name each byte of `id`
outside `[A-Za-z0-9._-]` is `%XX`. Kept `$SHED_SESSIONS_KEEP` days (default 30) after its last turn; `rm`
of its terminal deletes both at once.
